strong.notes: Default for substantive general work requiring strong reasoning, reliable coding, and tool use. GPT-6.1 Sol is the balanced intelligence/cost model. As a future-proof quota proxy, treat it as roughly 20x Luna's API cost and one-fifth of Astra's; escalate to Astra only when difficulty, ambiguity, or review stakes materially justify it.

strongest.cost: very high; ~100x Luna / 5x Sol API cost
strongest.notes: Use for exceptional scientific reasoning, the most rigorous technical or scientific reviews, or similarly consequential reasoning, including subtle cross-domain synthesis, when maximum reasoning quality is needed beyond what Sol is likely to provide. Select Astra directly when these criteria are met. As a future-proof quota proxy, treat it as roughly 5x GPT-6.1 Sol and 100x Luna by API price; otherwise prefer Sol or Luna.

workhorse.notes: Preferred for routine bounded implementation, inspection, testing, mechanical edits, and other focused high-volume work. Use Luna as the 1x API-cost/quota baseline; GPT-6.1 Sol is roughly 20x and Astra roughly 100x by API price. Escalate to Sol when substantial ambiguity, judgment, or task complexity appears.

alt-strongest.notes: Use selectively as an independent second perspective on difficult reasoning or review, especially when model-family diversity may expose blind spots. Do not spend the tighter Copilot allowance on routine work.

science-expensive.notes: Use for consequential scientific writing, discipline-sensitive critique, and major manuscript milestones only when Claude's writing or editorial strengths are specifically valuable and science-lite is unlikely to suffice. Its quota is extremely tight. For reasoning-led work, choose Luna, Sol, or Astra according to their role criteria rather than manuscript importance alone; prefer science-lite for bounded scientific prose.

science-lite.notes: Use for bounded scientific prose revision or focused manuscript critique where the main need is clarity, framing, or disciplinary conventions and Claude's strengths are useful. Route substantive scientific reasoning or validation of technical claims to Luna, Sol, or Astra according to their role criteria. Escalate to science-expensive only when its specialized writing or editorial strengths are needed beyond this role's scope. Prefer Luna for routine or non-scientific work.

free.notes: Use when preferred profiles are unavailable or a low-cost diversity check is useful. It is fast and free but quota-limited; do not rely on it for high-stakes conclusions.
